design.chain: Outbox -> RabbitMQ (quorum) -> Java consumer -> HTTP bridge -> real Python worker process -> WorkerEvent ingress -> settlement
design.broker: temporary rabbitmq:4.1.8-management container with random credentials on a loopback random port
design.worker_model: deterministic local model fixture (tests/platform_process_fixture.py); the worker process, HTTP contract, journal, heartbeat, artifact upload and accounting are real
design.source: local fixture tree in the worker fixture; egress allowlist, DNS and redirect controls are covered by unit tests instead
design.why_fixtures: this drill verifies platform coordination, so the model and repository contents are intentionally deterministic

cases.brokerDeliveryReachesARealWorkerAndASeco: first task SUCCEEDED on attempt 1 with one SETTLE ledger entry and a stored artifact; after killing the worker and starting a second process on the same fixed endpoint the next task also succeeds with its own single settlement and a consistent account
cases.aDeadLetteredDispatchIsRecoveredByTheNex: with no worker listening the delivery is refused until the dead-letter queue takes it; attempt and fence increase, no settlement is written, and the task only succeeds once a worker process is started and the coordinator republishes

tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: the worker fixture installed its deterministic model only on platform_worker, while platform_engine imports the client directly, so the engine tried the real provider and the process failed before any delivery could settle
tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.fix: patch both module bindings in backend/tests/platform_process_fixture.py
tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.note: the previous opt-in process test could not have passed with a clean environment before this fix

limitations: Single broker node and a single host: no cluster failover, no separate worker machine, no load balancer
The repository and model inside the worker are deterministic fixtures, so this is not evidence about model quality or egress control
A production audit that needs a real model still depends on provider behaviour; reasoning models can exhaust the per-call output cap
No capacity, latency-percentile or soak measurement
